A little history.

First, there was no web. Then the web began, and some asshole invented the banner ad. Well, not an asshole really. Everybody wants the web to be free, and you've got to monetize somehow. But anyway, advertisement was born on the internet.

This first wave of advertisement was all about attention. They got bigger, flashier, and more invasive. Flash started to be incorporated into little mini games. Lots of people started to do blinking moving pop-up ads. Sometimes they had sound. They got pretty terrible, people installed popup-blockers, browsers limited a lot of that sort of functionality, and that sort of died off... a little.

The next wave was/is all about targeting. People like Google and Facebook started to aggregate data about you, and than use that data to offer ads customized to your data profile. Overall, this was a pretty good innovation because it meant fewer, more modest ads that were more aligned to things you might be interested in. If any of those guys could be trusted not to give your information to the NAS, it would basically be an overall improvement.

The next wave is all about participation. Facebook is all up on this too, but it's this new evolution of the targeted ads that wants people to voluntarily subscribe to advertising impressions through social media.

Wave 1) IBM buys a certain number of banner ads in random places and pays for all of the times those ads were seen.

Wave 2) IBM buys targeted ads that get shown to people who's profile's suggest an interest those types of products.

Wave 3) IBM does an AMA, and people who have an active interest in IBM come to hear what IBM has to say, encouraged to "like" the IBM Facebook page.

Reddit is an investor-supported social media site, and investors have exactly one interest: make as much money as they can, however they can, whenever they can. If reddit looks like it can be flipped into a new-wave advertisement model, where they peddle corporate social media to consumers who volunteer to participate in their campaigns, that's exactly what they're going to do. And, if having a record of every click they're users have made is going to help them target the features of that agenda, then they're going to do that too.
